description.full: Hantu Raya, meaning \"Great Ghost\" or \"Grand Spirit,\" is one of the most powerful supernatural entities in Malay folklore and Islamic mysticism as practiced in Southeast Asia. Unlike ordinary hantu (ghosts), the Hantu Raya is an ancient, primordial spirit of immense power that can be bound and commanded by skilled practitioners known as bomoh or pawang. The spirit serves as a supernatural familiar, carrying out tasks ranging from protection and healing to more malevolent purposes depending on its master's intentions. In Malay-Islamic tradition, the Hantu Raya exists in the liminal space between Islamic cosmology's jinn and indigenous animist spirits. It is said to be invisible, capable of shapeshifting, and possessing knowledge of hidden things. The relationship between master and spirit is complex and dangerous, requiring constant vigilance and spiritual discipline. The Hantu Raya must be fed regular offerings, treated with respect, and controlled through proper Islamic invocations, or it may turn against its master with devastating consequences. The phenomenon represents a fascinating syncretism of pre-Islamic Malay animism with Islamic mystical practices, reflecting centuries of cultural and religious融合 in the Malay world. While orthodox Islamic authorities consider the practice of binding spirits to be problematic or forbidden, belief in Hantu Raya persists in both rural and urban Malay communities, demonstrating the enduring power of indigenous spiritual traditions within Islamic contexts.
